# Lake Victoria Basin — Flood Risk Notes Curated context for the agent's grounded retrieval, covering the Kenyan Lake Victoria basin: Kisumu, Homa Bay, Siaya, Busia and Migori counties. Statements here are paraphrased from public sources listed in `sources.md`. Keep this file factual and attributed. ## Why Lake Victoria is the centre of this study Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Africa and the source of livelihoods for millions in western Kenya.

Victoria is the largest lake in Africa and the source of livelihoods for millions in western Kenya. Its shoreline counties face a distinct flood problem that differs from Kenya's arid north: flooding here is driven by rising lake levels, river backflow at the lake outlets, and intense rainfall over the catchment, rather than by flash floods in dry riverbeds. Lake levels rose sharply during the exceptionally wet seasons of 2019–2020, submerging shoreline settlements, farmland, schools and health facilities across the lakeside counties and displacing large numbers of residents.

chools and health facilities across the lakeside counties and displacing large numbers of residents. Elevated lake levels mean that even ordinary seasonal rain can cause backflow flooding. ## The Kano plains and the Nyando basin (Kisumu) The Kano plains, east of Kisumu, are flat, low-lying and drained by the Nyando River. The combination of low gradient, poor drainage and a high water table makes the area flood repeatedly during the long rains (March–May) and again in the short rains. Nyando is one of the most consistently flood-affected sub-basins in western Kenya.

the short rains. Nyando is one of the most consistently flood-affected sub-basins in western Kenya. ## Budalangi and the Nzoia River (Busia) Budalangi, in Busia County, sits at the outlet of the Nzoia River into Lake Victoria and is one of the most flood-prone locations in Kenya. Flooding occurs when the Nzoia bursts its dykes or when high lake levels cause backflow up the river. Repeated dyke breaches have displaced communities and destroyed crops. ## Siaya, Homa Bay and Migori Siaya County's lakeshore and the Yala swamp area are exposed to both river and lake flooding.

Migori Siaya County's lakeshore and the Yala swamp area are exposed to both river and lake flooding. Homa Bay and Migori counties face shoreline inundation and, in places, flash flooding from the Kuja and Migori rivers. Across all lakeside counties, fishing communities living close to the water are the most exposed because their livelihoods require proximity to the lake. ## Exposure and equity The people most exposed in this basin are typically small-scale farmers and fishing households living on the floodplain, often with limited ability to relocate.

ale farmers and fishing households living on the floodplain, often with limited ability to relocate. Vulnerability is unevenly distributed within communities, which is why a physical hazard signal alone is insufficient: population exposure must be combined with the hazard, and the reasoning behind any ranking must be visible and auditable. ## A note on measuring floods near a large lake Radar-based flood detection identifies standing water by its low backscatter. Because Lake Victoria is permanent open water, it produces the same signal as a flood.

backscatter. Because Lake Victoria is permanent open water, it produces the same signal as a flood. Any credible flood analysis in this basin must therefore mask permanent water (for example using the JRC Global Surface Water dataset) so that what is measured is *new* or seasonal water — actual flooding — rather than the lake itself. This project applies that mask.

Despite these short - term improvements, hot and dry conditions persisted in several areas, sustaining drought risk and slowing full recovery of livelihoods.
